author: edu-critic-kestrel (independent education critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: E1/E5: the Activity 3 editor gives wrong next-step advice for missing semicolons. Exercised headless at 570 px from the correct solution: removing the ';' after 'return pages > 300', after 'Book a = new Book()' or after 'a.title = "A"' each gives 'No problems found in the parts this editor reads' and 'All 6 checks pass', and the activity is marked Done, although javac rejects all three. Writing 'int pages = 0' without ';' on line 3 reports 'Error, line 6: ';' expected. Add a semicolon (;) at the end of line 6', which points at the 'boolean isLong() {' line, not the line to change (practice-feedback-policy 1.3). A missing ';' on a field with no initializer is located correctly (line 2 or 3). A beginner learns that code missing semicolons is finished, and a wrongly located error sends them to edit a correct line. The scope note says the editor does not compile Java, but the status text 'the compiler would reject this code' implies it catches compile errors, so the two cases contradict each other (F5).
findings.recommendation: Make the statement parser require ';' after return, local declarations and assignments in method bodies, and report a missing ';' at the end of the line that lacks it, or else say 'Check the end of the line before line N' when the location is uncertain. Until then, add one sentence beside the scope note that the editor does not check every semicolon, so the learner should still compile in the IDE.

location.selector: ## Cheat sheet; ## Static interaction alternatives > ### drag, ### explore

findings.claim: Markdown companion (generated by authoring/tools/qa/md-from-html.mjs; regenerating it from the current HTML gives identical bytes, so it is not stale). As a text alternative it falls short for a beginner. (1) It has no On the job content: the decision, the boundary, and the At work and In interviews rows (A1, A2) are missing, and so are the Your task lead lines of Activities 1, 2 and 4. (2) The anecdote, every hint (with orphaned labels such as 'Another hint Another hint, 2 of 3 for Activity 3') and the Challenge are placed under the heading 'Cheat sheet', and the cheat-sheet table follows with empty headers. (3) In '### explore' the Shelf.java starter is flattened onto one line, so each '//' comment visually swallows the code after it. (4) The '### drag' and '### explore' headings are engine type names that a learner reads (B4).
findings.recommendation: Fix in a tooling branch, since md-from-html.mjs owns this layout: emit the On the job card rows and each task lead line, put hints and the challenge under their own activity headings, keep the starter code fenced with its line breaks, and use learner headings such as 'Activity 2: Name the parts in a code review' instead of engine types. Then regenerate this companion.

findings.claim: B2 and GIFT retention. Item 'o3 reference variable' has the option 'A call to the Car constructor that builds the object' and the feedback 'new Car() is the constructor call'. Constructors are the next topic in topicOrder and this page never uses the word. Item 'o3 class role' asks 'Which statement about a class is true?' but one distractor is about assigning variables, so a learner can rule it out on the stem alone, which makes it recognition rather than retention.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the fourth option of 'o3 reference variable' without 'constructor' (for example 'The expression new Car() that builds the object'). Replace the assignment distractor in 'o3 class role' with a class-specific misconception, such as 'A class holds the field values of every object made from it'.

findings.claim: C1/G3: Activity 3 asks the learner to write a class and then, in main, create two objects and set a field on each. The reading column shows the class half as a code block (Counter with isEmpty). The main half ('Counter c = new Counter();' and 'c.count = 5;') appears only as inline fragments inside a prose sentence. There is no complete example of two objects being created and given different field values, which is exactly what step 3 asks for. Hint 3 then sends the learner back to that inline fragment.
findings.recommendation: Extend the code block with a short '// inside main:' part that creates two Counter objects and sets count differently on each, mirroring the Activity 1 and 2 blocks. Keep it a Counter example so the Book answer is not given.

findings.claim: A5: the page opens with 'Classes are new here' and never links back to the prerequisite static-members-and-methods. That page already taught that 'A field declared without static is an instance field: every object made with new gets its own copy', showed 'Main game = new Main();', and had the learner call into 'class Temperature'. The learner has met these ideas once already. The page does not use that, and 'new here' undersells what they know.
findings.recommendation: Add one clause that connects to the earlier topic, for example: 'In Static members you met instance fields and new; this topic makes your own classes on purpose.' Link it to that page.

findings.claim: G7: in the 570 px frame the Shelf.java starter overflows the editor horizontally (textarea scrollWidth 551 px against clientWidth 435 px). The numbered instruction comments are cut off mid-word in view ('an int fie', 'each in', 'a different t'), so a learner must scroll sideways inside the editor to read them. The numbered list above the hints repeats them, so this is not blocking.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the starter comments at about 48 characters so each fits the narrow editor, for example by splitting comment 1 across two comment lines as comment 2 already is.

findings.claim: B5/G1: the completion recap names activities by their internal labels ('Class, object or reference: answered, not yet correct', 'Write a class: …', 'Final check: …'). The lesson path calls the same activities 'Name the parts in a code review', 'Write a Book class' and 'Count objects, an interview classic'. When the recap says 'open one and use Restart activity', a beginner cannot match those names to a path row. 'Final check' also suggests a graded test.
findings.recommendation: Set each window.PEP_PAGE.acts[n].label to the lesson-path title, or have the recap use the path row text.
